alice: Heads-up — ran a canary with FA v2.1 + paged-KV enabled; seeing a 15-20% p95 latency regression vs v2.0.

ben: Do you have the sampler/queue config for that run?

alice: Yep. It's the canary config we pushed yesterday: `batcher.sampler_window_ms=6`, `token_budget_target=1500`, `max_batch_tokens=4096`.

carol: Interesting. we usually use 12ms window on paged-KV workloads. Why did we reduce to 6?

alice: The change was to reduce client-side latency variance for small-seq traffic (PR #4321). It helped median but looks like it increased kernel churn on heavy-paged-kv traces.

perf-bot: [perf-bot] profile summary available: kernel_switches=87, avg_batch_tokens=920, p95_lat=312ms (+18%), page_faults=24, kv_paging_ratio=0.31

miriam: Kernel switches that high are suspicious. FA prefers larger contiguous KV, paged-KV forces different memory layout -> fallback/warmup. Could the smaller sampler window be increasing batch coalescing across heterogenous seq lengths?

ben: If sampler_window_ms is too small the batcher probes more often and starts batches with fewer queues but higher diversity in seq length. That can cause FlashAttention to pick hybrid kernels and trigger prefetch thrash.

alice: I grabbed a short flamegraph. Posting snippet: ```
# kernel selection trace (top)
0x01 - FlashAttention optimized path (40%)
0x02 - hybrid_attention (28%)
0x03 - paged_kv_prefetch (18%)
0x04 - mem_copy + fallback (14%)
```

carol: Hmm. Token budget target 1500 seems high for this traffic. Large token budgets + small windows -> batches get aggregated from multiple clients, increasing seq variance. Lowering token_budget_target to 800 might keep batches more homogeneous.

miriam: Agreed. Also try `max_batch_tokens=2048` for the canary. Keeps FlashAttention in its sweet spot for short-to-medium seqs.

ben: Can we reproduce quickly on the perf cluster? I'll spin up a replay with the same arrival trace and try three variants: (A) original 12ms/800/2048, (B) 6ms/1500/4096 (canary), (C) 6ms/800/2048.

alice: Run B is the one that regressed. If C matches A on p95, then sampler_window_ms reduction is fine but token_budget_target was the culprit.

perf-bot: [perf-bot] started replay job: replay-1745000000-1, ETA ~8m

ben: sharing the replay link: https://perf.internal/replays/replay-1745000000-1 :eyes:

miriam: Also add `runtime.flag: force_kernel_prefetch_threshold=0.25` for one run to see if we reduce paged-KV prefetch oscillation.

alice: noted. I'll watch the canary. If we see kernel_switches drop <40 and p95 back within 5%, we'll roll a hotfix changing token_budget_target and max_batch_tokens.

carol: Action: ben will run replays A/B/C + prefetch tweak. alice will collect traces and post flamegraphs. miriam will prepare a short rollback patch in case the canary keeps regressing.

ben: started run A now.

perf-bot: [perf-bot] replay-1745000000-1 completed: A(p95=260ms), B(p95=312ms), C(p95=265ms) — kernel_switches: A=32, B=88, C=34

alice: That's pretty conclusive. Token budget + max_batch_tokens combo caused cross-client batches that increased kernel switching and paged-KV thrash.

miriam: Ok let's ship a quick config change to the canary: `token_budget_target=800`, `max_batch_tokens=2048` and keep the reduced sampler window for the latency win.

carol: I'll add a note to the rollout checklist to watch kernel_switches and kv_paging_ratio metrics for 24h.

alice: Thanks team. Follow-up: we'll schedule a short perf postmortem with concrete heuristics for sampler_window_ms + token_budget interplay. :thumbsup:
